finding.text: F3 MEMORY COST OF A PENDING SOCKET IS NOT STATED (decision (c): documented minor; pre-existing, not part of this item). Probe h8.cjs: server in a child with --max-old-space-size=48, N sockets, each with a held first submit and ONE 64 KB block (1310 GETs) behind it: N=3, 5, 8, 12 survive (heap 18, 26, 27, 38 MB), N=24 dies (exit 134, out of memory); the accepted parent: 12 survive, 24 die. README line 117 (sealed) says nothing a client does can make memory grow without limit and cites a 48 MB child. True only as "bounded by the 128-connection cap times about 2 MB per pending socket". Follow-up: one README limit sentence (L-0213): what one pending socket costs and that the cap bounds it.
finding.followUp: README (limits, next to line 117): one sentence for L-0213: what one pending socket costs (about 2 MB per socket with a 64 KB block behind a held first request: a 48 MB child survives 12 and dies at 24, exit 134; identical on the accepted bytes) and that the 128-connection cap, not the tested heap, bounds it.
